_purpose: The reader's hand-edits, which are the one thing replaying the chapter cannot produce.
Anchored by prose, never by content: the edit body is the fenced block that follows the
anchor, read out of the chapter at run time. That is what stops this file going stale —
there is nothing here to fall out of step with the page, because the page is where the
bytes come from. Change the wording and the anchor stops resolving, which is an error.
An anchor must appear exactly once in its chapter. `verify-doc-output.py` fails if it
appears twice as loudly as if it appears never: an ambiguous anchor would silently pick

_why: State 2, and it cannot be a committed fixture. The chapter prints only the changed
@claim stanza, not the whole file — it is a fragment the reader pastes over one they
already have. A file assembled from it would not be the bytes the chapter prints,
which is the rule the whole arrangement rests on.
State 3 needs no entry at all: `fmt --write first.smy` produces it, and the chapter
prints that one as a *diff*. Deriving it by running the command is a stronger claim
than recording it would have been.
